correctness.rationale: Each explicit pair is chordal from simplicial clique attachments and connected, has the same degree-cell equitable quotient and is nonisomorphic by the multiplicities of the degree-two open neighbourhoods. For the minimum and census, deleting a simplicial vertex from a connected chordal graph preserves connectedness; this proves the exhaustive clique-attachment recurrence. Executed packaged checker enumerates 272 base seven-vertex graph-atlas representatives, 7268 clique extensions, 1614 exact-isomorphism classes at eight vertices, and then computes globally interned 1-WL tuple signatures, with verified stable vertex partitions and precisely two 2-member ambiguous classes; no ambiguous class exists on 1..7 vertices. Independent external ambient count of 1614 agrees with McKay; finite software dependencies and absence of independent code audit are explicitly disclosed.

value.rationale: The least order of failure of ordinary colour refinement within connected chordal graphs is a natural extremal invariant for a fundamental graph-isomorphism heuristic on a central perfect-elimination class. The complete first-collision census has only two types with distinct edge counts and explicit simple combinatorial representatives, explaining two mechanisms by which a cycle of simplicial attachments and duplicated matching attachments share all 1-WL colours. It is not a routine restatement of the unrestricted \(C^2\)/amenability classification, nor an arbitrary thin graph slice.
